full_judgment:
Mr. Mahmudul Amin Choudhury C. J. : This petition for leave to appeal is against judgment and order dated 13.8.1998 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3529 of 1998 making Rule absolute. 

 2. The short fact leading to this petition is that respondents are facing trial before the Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka on a Charge under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code in sessions Case No. 633 of 1996 which arose out of Gulshan P.S. Case No. 19(1)96. Respondents-accused filed the aforesaid Criminal Miscellaneous Case before the High Court Division under section 520 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking transfer of the aforesaid Sessions case from the Sessions Division Dhaka to any other court of competent jurisdiction in another Sessions Division around Dhaka. A Rule was issued accordingly. The ground on which the transfer petition was filed is that the accused persons had apprehension in their minds that they would be deprived of the opportunity of defending themselves in the court below and their apprehension is that the Judges in Dhaka Sessions Division have already formed opinion as regards merit of the case. In such circumstances the accused persons prayed for withdrawal of the aforesaid sessions case from Dhaka Sessions Davison and for its transfer to any other Sessions Division around Dhaka. The High Court Division then on hearing both the parties by judgment dated 13.8.1998 made the Rule absolute and ordered for withdrawal of the aforesaid sessions case from sessions Division Dhaka and transferred the same to the learned Sessions Judge, Narsingdi for trial. 

 3. Moulvi Md. Wahidullah, learned Advocate-on-Record appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the ground for which the petition under section 520 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed was not a proper and legal ground and on such a ground no case can be withdrawn from one Sessions Division and transferred to another Sessions Division. 

 4. We have gone through the judgment and it appears that before the High Court Division the learned Deputy Attorney General along with two other Lawyers appeared on behalf of the State who agreed for the transfer of the case from Dhaka Sessions Division to Narsingdi Sessions Division and when withdrawal was ordered on admission we find nothing to interfere with the same. In that view of the matter this petition is liable to be dismissed. But before we part with this matter we record our disnlea9m- in the 'way the Rule has been disposed of by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. The learned Judges wrote a very lengthy judgment unnecessarily on the question of withdrawal and transfer of such a case when the law has been settled long back. By writing such a lengthy judgment and incorporating certain decisions simply spoiled court's time in an unnecessary matter. When the State agreed on the transfer there was no reason or occasion to write such a lengthy judgment. It must be remembered that when the law is settled and when the State agreed on the transfer of the aforesaid case there was no need to write such a lengthy judgment spoiling court's valuable time.
